subject: english
question:
A sentence is provided in indirect speech. From the four given options, choose the one that most accurately conveys the sentence in its corresponding direct speech.
He said that he wished to speak with the manager.

options.text: "I wish to speak with the manager," he said.
"I want to speak with the manager," he said.
"I wished to speak with the manager," he said.
"May I speak with the manager?" he said.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** He said that he wished to speak with the manager.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **"he wished to speak" becomes "I wish to speak"**
 
 
• Pronoun "he" is converted to "I" to match direct speech.
 
• Verb "wished" is changed to "wish" to match the present tense in direct speech.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• Direct speech is enclosed in quotation marks.
 
• Starts with a capital letter "I" and ends with a period ".".
 
• Reporting clause follows the quoted speech, starting with a lowercase letter after the comma.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"“I wish to speak with the manager,” he said."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** "I want to speak with the manager," he said. 
 
 
• The word "want" changes the tone and meaning, suggesting a stronger desire rather than a polite wish.
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** "I wished to speak with the manager," he said. 
 
 
• Tense is incorrect: "wished" implies past, whereas the original sentence indicates a present wish.
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** "May I speak with the manager?" he said. 
 
 
• Changes the sentence into a question, altering the original statement format.
